# Lakkhaṇa Saṁyutta (SN 19)

**ID:** SN 19
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)

**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Linked Discourses with Lakkhaṇa

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Lakkhaṇa Saṁyutta* (SN 19) is a section of the *Saṁyuttanikāya* comprising discourses set around encounters between the monks Lakkhaṇa and Mahāmoggallāna [SuttaCentral; Hazra 1994]. While descending the mountain or walking for alms, Lakkhaṇa observes Moggallāna smile and questions him as to the reason [Asanga 2016; Hazra 1994]. In the presence of the Buddha and the monastic community, Moggallāna recounts that through his psychic powers he witnessed various disembodied apparitions or spirits (*peta*s) suffering agonizing torments in the sky [SuttaCentral; Tan 2002; Hazra 1994]. The Buddha confirms having seen the same apparitions during his own awakening and explains the precise karmic actions in their past lives that led to these retributions [Tan 2002; Anālayo 2017].

These vivid accounts of karmic retribution share nearly verbatim narrative passages with the Vinaya (*Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*, *Pārājika* 4 / Vin III 104–108), where DharmaNexus registers an extensive block of 569 matching segments totaling over 84,000 characters [Tan 2002; DharmaNexus]. Stories from the *Lakkhaṇa Saṁyutta* also provided material incorporated into the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* and bear strong thematic ties to the *Petavatthu* and *Vimānavatthu* [Tan 2002; Burlingame 1921; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus agree in identifying a full parallel series in the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (SĀ 508–528 in T 99) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of this text with the *Bieyi za ahan jing* (T 100) and Śamathadeva's Tibetan *Abhidharmakośaṭīkopayikā* (D4094) [DharmaNexus].
